sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: **Political Geography of India & World** covers territorial boundaries, states, union territories, international borders, capitals, and geopolitics.

Evolved continuously from the **Government of India Act 1935**, post-independence reorganization (**States Reorganisation Act 1956**), to recent formations like **Jammu & Kashmir Reorganization Act 2019**.
Indian subcontinent, South Asia region, neighboring countries, and strategic global political boundaries.
Examined by **UPSSSC** for candidates aspiring to Uttar Pradesh subordinate services.
Carries high weightage in **UPSSSC PET** under the General Awareness and Indian/World Geography syllabus.
Detailed breakdown of **28 States**, **8 Union Territories**, international boundary lines like **McMahon Line**, **Radcliffe Line**, and global country capitals.
Direct factual questions asked regarding neighbor countries, border lengths, capital cities, and state reorganization facts.

items.title: 1. India's Land Neighbors and Border Lengths
items.content:
• Shares land borders with **7 countries**.
• Longest land border: **Bangladesh** (**4,096.7 km**).
• Shortest land border: **Afghanistan** (**106 km**).
• **Mnemonic for Length Order:** "**BCCB MNA**"
• **B**angladesh > **C**hina > **P/Pakistan** > **N/Nepal** > **M**yanmar > **Bhutan** > **A**fghanistan.

items.title: 2. Indian States Touching International Borders
items.content:
• **Pakistan (4 States/UTs):** Jammu & Kashmir, Ladakh, Punjab, Rajasthan, Gujarat.
• **China (5 States/UTs):** Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh.
• **Nepal (5 States):** Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, Sikkim.
• **Bangladesh (5 States):** West Bengal, Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram.
• **Myanmar (4 States):** Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram.

items.title: 3. Important International Boundary Lines
items.content:
• **Radcliffe Line:** India and **Pakistan** (drawn in 1947 by Sir Cyril Radcliffe).
• **McMahon Line:** India (Arunachal Pradesh) and **China**.
• **Durand Line:** Pakistan and **Afghanistan** (India shares with Pak/PoK).
• **Line of Control (LoC):** De facto military border between India and Pakistan in Kashmir.
• **Line of Actual Control (LAC):** Effective demarcation line between India and China.

items.title: 4. Indian States Reorganisation Milestones
items.content:
• **Dhar Commission (1948):** Recommended reorganization on administrative convenience, not linguistic.
• **JVP Committee (1948-49):** Jawaharlal Nehru, Vallabhbhai Patel, Pattabhi Sitaramayya rejected linguistic basis initially.
• **Fazl Ali Commission (1953):** Accepted language as the basis of reorganization.
• **States Reorganisation Act (1956):** Created **14 States** and **6 Union Territories** on Nov 1, 1956.

items.title: 5. Union Territories and Capitals of India
items.content:
• Total States: **28** | Total Union Territories: **8**.
• **Andaman & Nicobar:** Port Blair
• **Chandigarh:** Chandigarh
• **Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu:** Daman
• **Delhi:** New Delhi
• **Jammu & Kashmir:** Srinagar (Summer), Jammu (Winter)
• **Ladakh:** Leh
• **Lakshadweep:** Kavaratti
• **Puducherry:** Puducherry

items.title: 6. Tropic of Cancer Passing Through Indian States
items.content:
• Passes through **8 Indian states**.
• **Mnemonic:** "**CHJ RAM PB**" or "**MR. JCP BHABU**"
• **States:** **G**ujarat, **R**ajasthan, **M**adhya Pradesh, **C**hhattisgarh, **J**harkhand, **W**est Bengal, **T**ripura, **M**izoram.

items.definition: Use **'MB CA PBN'** (Maa Baap Children Aur Party Bahut Nonstop): **M**angladesh, **B**hutan (wait use actual: **B**angladesh, **C**hina, **P**akistan, **N**epal, **M**yanmar, **B**hutan, **A**fghanistan).
Use **'PRAM GJ CWB'** or sentence: **'Guruji's RAJ-M-C JHA-T-M movie'**: **G**ujarat, **R**ajasthan, **M**adhya Pradesh, **C**hhattisgarh, **J**harkhand, **W**est Bengal, **T**ripura, **M**izoram.
UP shares borders with **8 states** and **1 UT** (Delhi). States: **UK, HP, Haryana, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Bihar, Jharkhand**.

items.term: Trick 4: Seven Sister States of Northeast
items.definition: Use **'ATM MM NA'**: **A**ssam, **T**ripura, **M**eghalaya, **M**anipur, **M**izoram, **N**agaland, **A**runachal Pradesh. (Sikkim is a brother, not a sister).
Use **'UP BI-SU-WE'**: **U**ttar **P**radesh, **Bi**har, **Su**ttarakhand (Uttarakhand), **Si**kkim, **We**st Bengal.
Use **'AM-ME-TR-MI-WB'**: **A**ssam, **Me**ghalaya, **Tr**ipura, **Mi**zoram, **W**est **B**engal.
Students think India does not touch Afghanistan directly. Fact: India shares a **106 km** border with Afghanistan in PoK (Ladakh sector).
Students include Sikkim in Northeast Seven Sister states. Fact: Sikkim is **NOT** one of the Seven Sisters; it is part of the North-Eastern Council (NEC) but distinct.

items.term: Mistake 3: Tropic of Cancer and UP
items.definition: Students often believe the Tropic of Cancer passes through Uttar Pradesh. Fact: It passes through **Madhya Pradesh and Jharkhand**, but **NOT** Uttar Pradesh.
Students confuse China with Bangladesh. Fact: India's longest land border is with **Bangladesh** (4,096.7 km), followed by China.
Students write 7 or 9 UTs due to outdated GK books. Fact: After Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu merger, and J&K bifurcation, total UTs are **8**.
Students write Colombo as the sole administrative capital. Fact: **Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte** is the official legislative/administrative capital.

upscNotes.content: For UPSSSC PET, memorize exact border lengths and order of neighboring countries from largest to smallest, as direct ranking questions frequently appear.
Examiners often trap students by asking whether the Tropic of Cancer passes through UP or Bihar. Remember it touches neither; it passes through Jharkhand and MP.
Keep track of the latest Union Territory mergers and Jammu & Kashmir reorganization details as questions on current political map updates are common.
Do not confuse the Durand line with the Radcliffe line when questions mention Afghanistan-Pakistan or India-Pakistan boundaries.

keyTakeaways: India shares land borders with 7 nations, with Bangladesh being the longest and Afghanistan the shortest.
The Tropic of Cancer passes through 8 Indian states, excluding Uttar Pradesh.
India has 28 States and 8 Union Territories as per current administrative divisions.
Radcliffe Line separates India-Pakistan, and McMahon Line separates India-China.
India's Standard Meridian is 82.5° E longitude, passing through Mirzapur, UP.
States Reorganisation Act of 1956 reorganized states on a linguistic basis.
